chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Al-Hasan ibn Salih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

a man who bequeathed to his slave one-third of his wealth, he said, and he said: 'The slave is appraised at a fair price, then it is looked at what is one-third of the deceased's estate. If the one-third is less than the value of the slave by the amount of a quarter of the value, the slave is freed for that quarter of the value. And if the one-third is more than the value of the slave, the slave is freed and what remains of the one-third after the value is given to him.' And this news does not contradict what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: How is a slave's emancipation calculated when bequeathed one-third of an estate?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of partial manumission by appraising the slave's value against the one-third bequest, ensuring that if the share is insufficient, the slave is freed proportionally to the amount paid, while any surplus is retained by the slave. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the slave's right to acquire freedom through their bequest, balancing the estate's distribution with the emancipation process. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the financial mechanics of 'kitabah' and partial manumission in Islamic inheritance law.
